no_business_rules_reason: CBSTM03B is a file-access subroutine for CBSTM03A. Based on the DD name and operation code passed in LK-M03B-AREA it opens, reads (sequentially or by key) or closes one of four indexed files and returns the file status in LK-M03B-RC. It makes no business decisions; its conditional logic is only the dispatch on file name and operation code.

no_rule_decisions.reason: Technical dispatch on the DD name requested by the caller (TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE); unknown names simply GOBACK.
Dispatch on operation code (open, sequential read, close) for TRNXFILE; pure I/O.
Dispatch on operation code (open, sequential read, close) for XREFFILE; pure I/O.
Dispatch on operation code (open, keyed read, close) for CUSTFILE; pure I/O.
Dispatch on operation code (open, keyed read, close) for ACCTFILE; pure I/O.

observations.text: For an unknown DD name the routine GOBACKs without setting LK-M03B-RC, so the caller sees whatever it pre-loaded (CBSTM03A moves ZERO, i.e. '00' = success).

Operation codes declared but not implemented (M03B-WRITE 'W', M03B-REWRITE 'Z', and keyed/sequential reads on the 'wrong' file) fall through to the exit paragraph and return the previous file status, which can look like success.

TRNXFILE is keyed by FD-TRNXS-ID = card number (16) + transaction id (16), so a sequential read returns transactions ordered by card number; CBSTM03A relies on this order when grouping transactions by card.

paragraphs.logic: EVALUATEs LK-M03B-DD and performs the matching file routine (1000 TRNXFILE, 2000 XREFFILE, 3000 CUSTFILE, 4000 ACCTFILE) THRU its x999 exit; any other DD name goes to 9999-GOBACK.
paragraphs.name: 0000-START

paragraphs.logic: For TRNX-FILE: on M03B-OPEN opens it for input, on M03B-READ reads the next record into LK-M03B-FLDT, on M03B-CLOSE closes it; each branch jumps to 1900-EXIT.
paragraphs.name: 1000-TRNXFILE-PROC

paragraphs.logic: End of the TRNXFILE PERFORM THRU range (EXIT).
paragraphs.name: 1999-EXIT

paragraphs.logic: For XREF-FILE: on M03B-OPEN opens it for input, on M03B-READ reads the next record into LK-M03B-FLDT, on M03B-CLOSE closes it; each branch jumps to 2900-EXIT.
paragraphs.name: 2000-XREFFILE-PROC

paragraphs.logic: End of the XREFFILE PERFORM THRU range (EXIT).
paragraphs.name: 2999-EXIT

paragraphs.logic: For CUST-FILE: on M03B-OPEN opens it for input; on M03B-READ-K moves LK-M03B-KEY(1:LK-M03B-KEY-LN) to FD-CUST-ID and reads randomly into LK-M03B-FLDT; on M03B-CLOSE closes it; each branch jumps to 3900-EXIT.
paragraphs.name: 3000-CUSTFILE-PROC

paragraphs.logic: End of the CUSTFILE PERFORM THRU range (EXIT).
paragraphs.name: 3999-EXIT

paragraphs.logic: For ACCT-FILE: on M03B-OPEN opens it for input; on M03B-READ-K moves LK-M03B-KEY(1:LK-M03B-KEY-LN) to FD-ACCT-ID and reads randomly into LK-M03B-FLDT; on M03B-CLOSE closes it; each branch jumps to 4900-EXIT.
paragraphs.name: 4000-ACCTFILE-PROC

paragraphs.logic: End of the ACCTFILE PERFORM THRU range (EXIT).
paragraphs.name: 4999-EXIT

summary.text: CBSTM03B is a batch COBOL subroutine called by the statement program CBSTM03A to perform all file I/O. The caller passes a DD name (TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE or ACCTFILE), an operation code (O open, R sequential read, K keyed read, C close), an optional key and key length. The routine opens the file for input, reads the next record (transaction and cross-reference files, sequential) or reads by key (customer and account files, random), or closes it, returning the record in the 1000-byte LK-M03B-FLDT area and the two-byte file status in LK-M03B-RC. It writes no files and performs no business logic.
